handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For blumira the manifest gained: BLUMIRA_BASE_URL. server.json gained: BLUMIRA_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: BLUMIRA_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The hand-written `auth login` novel (internal/cli/auth_login.go: client_credentials mint against auth.blumira.com) still declares flag provenance to the press-native MarkCredentialsExplicit, so a credential inherited from BLUMIRA_CLIENT_ID/BLUMIRA_CLIENT_SECRET is never written to config.toml; this entry also keeps the file alive through the fleet replay.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 made env-oauth-secrets-not-persisted native (SaveTokens keeps the env markers and the press generates MarkCredentialsExplicit), so the fleet replay retires that entry. Its asserts were the only ones naming cli/internal/cli/auth_login.go, and replay_handfixes.py deletes every hand-written file that only a retired entry pinned ('a retired hand-fix's own file'). auth_login.go is not a test of the hand-fix: it is the connector's only way to mint a JWT (novel feature 'Self-minting OAuth2 auth login'). On the 4.35.1 reprint the replay deleted it and the build failed (root.go: undefined newNovelAuthLoginCmd). The press-native MarkCredentialsExplicit only helps if the one caller that receives flags passes provenance, which is this file; the asserts pin that call so the env secret stays off disk.

handfixes.summary: sync keeps the partition names every published store uses: /org/users syncs as `org` and /org/agents/devices as `org-agents-devices` (press 4.35.1 renders them as `org-users` and `org`).
handfixes.why: Press 4.35.1 re-derived the org partition names: devices moved into `org` and users into a new `org-users`, with every gate green. The dc-roster and exposure novels and the shared analytics engine read `org-agents-devices`, so on the raw render they reported zero devices; and an existing 4.24.0 store keeps users under `org`, so devices synced into `org` would mix with stale user rows that a domain-controller rollup would misread. bin/resource_names.py (cli-factory/blumira/reprint-4351-20261102) swaps the two keys back in the partition tables only (sync.go maps and cases, channel_workflow.go, data_source.go, learn_init.go, and store.go's resourceIDFieldOverrides), leaving the typed-table UpsertOrg route on `org` as published. Spec cannot pin it: x-pp-resource forces a flat resource and renames the command path. The swap must not touch reconcileTypedTables: it is keyed by the partition UpsertBatch writes into each typed table, and UpsertOrg's typed table `org` holds /org/users rows, so it stays `"org": "org"`. Swapping it there (codex review r1) made `sync --full` prune of org-agents-devices fail with "no such table: org-agents-devices", leaving removed devices in exposure/dc-roster, and left pruned users in the typed table; reconcile_typed_table_test.go prunes every partition and fails on that swap (logs/seen-r1-reconcile-typed-table-fails.log).

handfixes.summary: `auth login` sends the client secret only to the configured token endpoint: its mint client refuses every redirect, and the press's GuardTokenRequest refuses a plaintext (non-loopback http) token URL before dialing.
handfixes.why: The novel minted with http.DefaultClient, which follows 301/302/307/308; a 307/308 replays the POST body, client_secret included, to whatever host Location names (proven: internal/cli/auth_login_redirect_test.go TestMintRefusesEveryRedirect failed on the published code for all four codes, and the secret reached the second server on 307 and 308). Host pinning stays connector-owned under the credential kit. The novel also accepted --auth-url http://<remote>, sending the secret in cleartext; GuardTokenRequest (4.35.1 client) now refuses it (TestMintRefusesPlaintextRemoteTokenURL, seen failing with the guard removed).

handfixes.summary: Every typed MCP endpoint tool that is not read-only (assign owners, add a comment, resolve a finding; org and MSP sub-account) returns a preview and sends nothing until confirm is boolean true
handfixes.why: Work-order rule: every MCP write previews and sends only with confirm: true. At 4.35.1 (and in the published 0.1.6) the six generated endpoint write tools sent on the first call. The gate wraps every registered non-read-only, non-mirrored tool, so an endpoint a later print adds is gated too (abnormal/skykick/connectwise-automate precedent). A recipe intent over a command annotated mcp:read-only is marked read-only instead of gated (find_unprotected_domain_controllers over exposure). blumira_endpoint_confirm_test.go proves an unconfirmed call reaches the server 0 times and a confirmed one once (seen failing unwired: logs/seen-endpoint-confirm-fails.log); blumira_confirm_registered_test.go fails on the unwired tools.go (logs/seen-confirm-fails.log).

handfixes.why: The 4.35.1 render sends limit=200 as the page size, but Blumira's page size is page_size (spec default 50) and limit caps the whole list. Every page then held 50 rows, 50 < 200 read as the natural end, and sync stored the first 50 rows of every partition with sync_state.last_attempt_complete = 1, so device coverage, triage and every count over 50 rows were wrong and reported as complete (TestR2SyncFollowsDocumentedPaging, seen failing on the scaffold commit). handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal, both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit, every HTTP client (API, auth login token mint, --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport, every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers, every program file write through the kit, child processes through credkit.RunCommand, and the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP. The credential store, config.toml and the Spacefast delivery record are sources, written outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile).
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the per-connector credential layer this connector never had. Classes the print review left for the kit, closed and each proven by a built-binary test seen failing first on the pre-kit build (internal/credwire/leak_test.go): the token endpoint's error text repeating the client secret, and the client secret sent to an --auth-url other than https://auth.blumira.com (TestTokenEndpointEchoNeverPrints); an API page's error field repeating the bearer, copied into sync errors, msp_account_device_coverage.error and exposure/dc-roster rows (TestPagerErrorEchoNeverReachesStoreOrOutput); a profiles.json value under a credential flag's name held at startup (TestProfileCredentialValueHeldAtStartup). The learn journal is appended with credkit.AppendFile. feedback --stdin keeps its body (compactStdinBody / RestoreFeedbackStdin, TestFeedbackStdinIsRecorded). In-process tests never run Start, so cliutil.OutboundGuard, Hold and HoldBody are variables the test seams swap (credkit_seam_test.go in internal/cli and internal/mcp). The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to the _length_limit DSN parameter, and openReadOnlySQLite runs select 1 because the kit's connection does not forward Ping.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
